project: Compute Fund — first UI page exploration
brief: First UI page of Compute Fund, a Kickstarter-inspired crowdfunding platform where patrons (never investors) fund LLM compute tokens — fiat or crypto. Every compute run issues a public receipt (model, tokens, cost, output). Community votes milestones; language is patronage, not investment. Each candidate shows the same first screen: project grid with funding progress toward goal ($7,420/$12,000, $3,120/$6,800, $8,910/$9,500) and patron tier buttons ($25/$100/$500). Same content and primary action (fund a run), three different visual languages, all evolving away from the deep-green v0 baseline.

candidates.name: v0 Baseline (现状) — Deep Green Cards
candidates.concept: Current state: friendly light-neutral dashboard, deep-green primary, 3-col project card grid with thin progress bar and 3-button footer. Kept as the reference point every direction must evolve from, not repeat.
candidates.typography: System UI sans (Segoe/Helvetica), weights 400/600; 11px uppercase tracked chips, 17–24px semibold headings, 13–14px body. No display face.
traits: Light warm-grey page, white cards
Thin 8px rounded progress bar
Chip-style category labels
Uniform 3-button card footers
Soft 8px radius everywhere

candidates.name: 01 — Carbon Ledger
candidates.concept: The platform's radical-transparency ethos as a physical document: each project entry reads like an auditable carbon-audit ledger card filed in a public record — dotted leader lines, entry items, a stamped seal, hatched ink bar. Using it feels like reading a trustworthy filing cabinet, not a storefront.
candidates.typography: Serif-led editorial register: Iowan Old Style / Georgia for project titles, headings and body (700 titles 21px, body 14px); mono (SF Mono/Consolas) for every number, ledger line and label, 10–12px, letterspaced smallcaps feel.
traits: Aged-paper field with faint ruled texture
Dashed perforation rules at card top/bottom
Dotted leader lines between label and value
45° hatched ink progress bar with mono % overlay
Double-rule masthead with red seal accents

candidates.name: 02 — Public Address
candidates.concept: The community decides — so the page shouts like civic street media: a public noticeboard / kiosk poster wall where the funding percentage itself is the headline. Community-priority status is treated as a public tag, patrons replace backers everywhere. Using it feels like standing in front of a wall of serious civic posters.
candidates.typography: Heavy poster display: Archivo Black / Arial Black uppercase condensed headings (56px percent figures, 19–30px titles); Work Sans for one-line summaries (13px); mono uppercase 10–11px for metadata, receipts and legend.
traits: 3px black borders on every element, wheat-paper grain
Percent figure is the hero of each card
Block-segment funding bar (each block = a funding chunk)
Blue civic category tags overlapping card frame
Black poster-strip headers like kiosk notices

candidates.name: 03 — Terminal Commons
candidates.concept: The public receipt IS the interface: one compute commons wall where each project is a live unit streaming its most recent public receipts (run, model, spend, output) in phosphor green on near-black. Radical transparency becomes ambience — you watch the commons work. Using it feels like standing at the master control panel of shared machine-time.
candidates.typography: Mono-led instrument register: system mono (JetBrains/SF Mono/Consolas) for the receipt streams, status bar, tiers, ticker and all numbers (11px, 1.7 line-height); Inter/system sans only for unit titles (16px semibold) — sans is the voice of people, mono is the voice of the machine.
traits: Phosphor-green amber-and-red signal palette on near-black panels
Live receipt stream block per card (run, model, −cost, output)
Amber priority and unit IDs; green confirmed outputs
Glowing gauge percent + thin neon progress bar
Bottom live-ledger ticker strip

01-carbon-ledger.audience: Researchers, grant officers, auditable-minded patrons who distrust marketing surfaces
01-carbon-ledger.hero: The ledger card itself — dotted-leader entry lines and the hatched ink progress bar
01-carbon-ledger.motion_note: Paper feel: numbers settle like typewriter strikes when a new run is receipted; the hatched bar fills with a subtle ink-bleed ease; stamping a commitment presses the seal down 2px with a spring release. One hero move: on each new compute receipt, a stamped line types itself into the card.

02-public-address.audience: The broad crowd — first-visit first-time backers, community voters, people moved by civic urgency
02-public-address.hero: The giant funding-percent figure as poster headline, backed by the block-segment bar
02-public-address.motion_note: Poster behavior: percent figures roll up like a split-flap display on load; each bar block fills with a firm snap (200ms, no bounce) as funding ticks; community-priority tag flips in with a single rotateX. One hero move: when a project crosses 100%, its whole poster border flashes red for one beat — the kiosk 'funded' moment.

03-terminal-commons.audience: Builders, agents-economy natives, technical patrons watching the compute commons live
03-terminal-commons.hero: The streaming public-receipt block inside each unit plus the glowing green gauge
03-terminal-commons.motion_note: Instrument behavior: receipt lines stream in top-to-bottom with a 30ms cascade; the status-bar patron counter ticks up live; the gauge glow pulses once per confirmed run (single 600ms breathe, no loops). One hero move: funding the run appends a new line into the live stream — 'patron +$100 · run queued' — so the user sees themselves enter the public record.
